stories.title: ColRich Pays $52.4M for Mesa Rental Community
stories.excerpt: ColRich acquired Avia 266, a 267-unit multifamily community in Mesa, AZ, for $52.4 million, including the assumption of an existing HUD loan. The buyer intends to rename the property The Remy. The sales price comes out to just under $200,000 a unit. Geringer Capital was the seller. Geringer paid $45.25 million for the property in 2019. CBRE’s Matt Pesch, Asher Gunter and Austin Groen represented Geringer. Completed in 1984, Avia 266 features a low-density garden site plan with all one- and two-bedroom units. Community amenities include two pool and spa areas, a 24/7 fitness center, an outdoor courtyard with recreation and gathering spaces, a resident clubhouse with community kitchen, package lockers, and a fenced dog park. Mesa Riverview shopping center, the Riverview Baseball Complex, Riverview Park, and the spring training home for Major League Baseball’s Chicago Cubs at Sloan Park are within walking distance of Avia 266. bullets: ColRich acquired Avia 266, 267-unit Mesa garden community, for $52.4M ($196.6K/unit).

stories.summary: ColRich purchased Avia 266, a 267-unit garden-style multifamily community in Mesa, Arizona, for $52.4 million (including HUD loan assumption), valuing units at under $200,000 each. The property, built in 1984 and featuring all one- and two-bedroom units, was sold by Geringer Capital, which acquired it for $45.25 million in 2019—a 15.8% appreciation over six years. The community benefits from proximity to MLB spring training and retail shopping.
stories.impact: Sub-$200K/unit pricing in Mesa despite minimal recent value creation signals softening Phoenix-area demand or cap-rate compression in secondary metros. The modest arbitrage (6-year hold at <16% total return) suggests limited rent growth tailwinds in Phoenix proper; developers should monitor whether speculative capital is still chasing underperforming garden-style assets in the submarket.

stories.title: Blue Owl Capital Provides $106M to Refi Lowell Hotel in New York City
stories.excerpt: A historic New York City hotel has received a new round of debt financing. Kensico Properties has secured $106 million to refinance the Lowell Hotel, a 17-story, 74-key luxury boutique hotel on Manhattan’s Upper East that the firm purchased and redeveloped in 1984, Commercial Observer can first report. Blue Owl Capital provided the senior loan, which will replace existing debt, while CBRE’s Matthew Klauer arranged the transaction on behalf of Kensico Properties. “The Lowell represents one of the most storied and irreplaceable luxury hospitality assets in the United States,” said Klauer. “The hotel’s unmatched reputation, superior market position, and experienced ownership group made this an exceptional lending opportunity.” Located at 28 East 63rd Street just off the corner of Madison Avenue and a few blocks from Central Park, The Lowell Hotel opened in 1927. The hotel features 74 guest rooms and suites, many of which include private terraces, and features notable bars like the Club Room and the Pembroke Room. Brian Pascus can be reached at bpascus@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Blue Owl Capital refinanced Lowell Hotel (NYC, 74-key luxury boutique) with $106M senior loan.
Historic Upper East Side asset at 28 E 63rd St.; hospitality, not multifamily.
Loan replaces existing debt; CBRE arranged transaction for Kensico Properties.
stories.summary: Kensico Properties secured a $106 million senior refinance from Blue Owl Capital for the Lowell Hotel, a 17-story luxury boutique hotel on Manhattan's Upper East Side with 74 guest keys, originally opened in 1927 and redeveloped by Kensico in 1984. The facility replaces existing debt and was arranged by CBRE's Matthew Klauer.
stories.impact: Not material to multifamily development. Hospitality debt market tightness/repricing affects different capital stacks and investor bases; no direct signal on apartment supply, demand, or cost dynamics.

stories.title: Salad and Go Shutters All 60 Arizona Locations
stories.excerpt: Salad and Go, a made-to-order fast-casual spot dishing up salads, wraps and breakfast options, has filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy and revealed all locations will close down immediately. Founded in Gilbert, the chain has more than 60 stores in Arizona as well as a large distribution center on 27th Avenue in Phoenix. The co-founders of Salad and Go exited back in 2021 after selling to an investment firm. The distressed financial situation of the company was exacerbated by the recent Cyclospora scare. In a company release, the company said, “The Cyclospora outbreak in July, in which Salad and Go was not implicated, weakened confidence across the industry and compounded these challenges.” The company had been steadily closing locations before the latest announcements. The Chapter 11 process will provide Salad and Go a court-supervised framework for the company to realize the value of its assets and to meet its obligations. stories.summary: Salad and Go, a made-to-order fast-casual restaurant chain with over 60 locations across Arizona and a major distribution center in Phoenix, filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy and announced immediate closure of all stores. The company blamed a July Cyclospora outbreak in the industry (though not directly implicating Salad and Go) for eroding consumer confidence and compounding pre-existing financial stress.
stories.impact: Modest signal for Phoenix multifamily: loss of 60+ retail/QSR tenants and a significant distribution footprint reduces mixed-use development appeal and retail-ground-floor leasing velocity in Phoenix. However, broader impact is limited unless the closures free up prime retail real estate for adaptive reuse or mixed-income housing in infill submarkets like downtown Phoenix or Scottsdale.

stories.title: AI Song Maker Suno Takes 12K SF at 515 West 20th Street
stories.excerpt: We can discuss the ethics of artificial intelligence creating art all day long, but the fact is these companies aren’t going anywhere anytime soon, and they need office space. Generative AI music platform Suno has taken 12,048 square feet across the fifth floor of 515 West 20th Street for its first New York City office, Commercial Observer has learned. Michael Segerman at Current Real Estate Advisors represented the landlord, Justin Amirian’s Eagle Point Properties, while Joseph Sipala from JLL represented Suno. JLL did not immediately respond to CO’s request for comment. The asking rent and the length of the lease were not disclosed. However, asking rents at 515 West 20th Street are in the high $30s per square foot, CO previously reported. The seven-story West Chelsea building sits just west of the High Line, a short distance from the Hudson River. “Some of the executives are tied to the area,” Segerman said of why Suno chose this space for its office. “They really like West Chelsea, and we’re also seeing a large influx of AI tenants moving into this pocket submarket of New York City. We signed another 6,000 square feet to another AI tenant in the building just just two weeks ago. So we’re seeing a lot of AI movement in the pocket of this submarket of West Chelsea.” Suno did not immediately respond to CO’s request for comment. The AI company recently lost a copyright infringement lawsuit to the German licensing agency GEMA, according to Reuters. The verdict determined that Suno, which works by creating songs based on information users add to prompts, violated copyrights by processing songs by artists GEMA represents. The court ruled Suno will have to pay damages that have yet to be determined. In June, AI firm Isara Laboratories took 6,009 square feet at the mixed-use building at 515 West 20th Street. bullets: Suno (AI music platform) leased 12,048 SF at 515 West 20th St, NYC (5th floor).
West Chelsea office space; asking rents in high $30s/SF; lease terms not disclosed.
AI/generative tech company expansion; executives drawn to West Chelsea location preference.
stories.summary: Suno, a generative AI music platform, leased 12,048 square feet on the fifth floor of 515 West 20th Street in Manhattan's West Chelsea for its first New York City office. The seven-story building sits just west of the High Line; asking rents are in the high $30s per square foot. Current Real Estate Advisors represented the landlord (Eagle Point Properties); JLL represented Suno.
stories.impact: Not material to multifamily. Office leasing by tech firms signals continued NYC-based employment demand, which supports residential occupancy and rent growth; however, this is an isolated 12K SF deal and doesn't move apartment supply or development fundamentals materially. Monitor broader AI-sector hiring in NYC as a longer-term residential demand tailwind.

stories.title: Ultimate Equity Buys Hollywood, Fla., Townhouse Project for $32M
stories.excerpt: Ultimate Equity has acquired a 69-unit townhome community in Hollywood, Fla., for $32 million, Cushman & Wakefield announced. The gated community called Royal Oaks in the Emerald Hills neighborhood changed hands in an all-cash 1031 exchange acquisition at a record price per unit for the submarket, and a capitalization rate below 5 percent, Cushman & Wakefield said. An entity named Royal Oak TH, run by Preston Giuliano Capital Partners, sold the property for about 36 percent more than what they paid to acquire it less than 12 months ago. Records with Preston Giuliano Capital Partners show the property last sold for $23.5 million in August 2025. Built in 2009 at 3200 Stirling Road, Royal Oaks comprises 13 buildings totaling 116,886 square feet across a 5.1-acre site. Each unit includes three bedrooms and 2.5 bathrooms in 1,694 square feet, with a private garage. Monthly rents range from $3,228 to $3,281, according to the Royal Oaks website. Community amenities include a clubhouse, pool and picnic area. Virgilio Fernandez and Mitash Kripalani of Cushman & Wakefield brokered the sale. “Assets like Royal Oaks practically never come to market in Emerald Hills,” Fernandez said in a statement. “It is a gated, for-rent townhome community in one of Hollywood’s most desirable and supply constrained neighborhoods. Running a disciplined off-market process, we were able to close quickly on an all-cash 1031 basis and deliver a record price per unit for the seller at a cap rate below 5 percent.” Ultimate Equity, owned by David Sedaghati, who operates footwear maker Ultimate Shoes, is an active player in the region, and sold a development site in Miami’s Wynwood neighborhood in March for $54 million. Jeff Ostrowski can be reached at jostrowski@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Ultimate Equity acquired Royal Oaks, 69-unit townhome community, Hollywood Fla., for $32M.
All-cash 1031 exchange; record price per unit for Emerald Hills submarket (~$464K/unit).
Seller flipped property 36% in under 12 months (bought $23.5M Aug 2025); cap rate below 5%.
stories.summary: Ultimate Equity purchased Royal Oaks, a 69-unit gated townhome community in Hollywood, Florida's Emerald Hills neighborhood, for $32 million in an all-cash 1031 exchange acquisition. The seller (Royal Oak TH/Preston Giuliano Capital Partners) realized a 36% profit in less than 12 months, having acquired the property for $23.5 million in August 2025. The transaction represents a record price per unit (~$464K) and cap rate below 5% for the submarket. Units feature 3BR/2.5BA, private garages, and rents of $3,228–$3,281/month.
stories.impact: Extremely tight cap rates (sub-5%) and rapid 36% flips in South Florida townhome sector signal frothy valuations driven by yield-starved capital and strong rental demand. For developers: low-cap-rate trades and repeat quick-flip activity suggest limited upside and increased refinance/extension risk; focus on primary South Florida markets (Miami-Dade, Broward) for new supply where rental growth can sustain sub-5% initial yields. Monitor if cash-buyer dominance is masking weaker financing availability.

stories.title: TCU Proceeding with 2,500-Bed Campus Housing Development
stories.excerpt: Texas Christian University, American Campus Communities(ACC), and The Beck Group, marked a key topping out milestone for an on-campus residential development. The new residential community will deliver more than 2,500 beds across a mix of modern first-year residence halls and townhome-style housing for sophomores. The community is expected to open in fall 2027. It’s designed in partnership with Robert A.M. Stern Architects. The project will be delivered through a third-party, fee-based development structure. TCU will maintain institutional ownership. Pod-style residence halls will foster community-building for first-year students, while townhomes will offer upper-division students greater independence. Construction remains on schedule, with the new residential community expected to welcome students for the Fall 2027 semester. The topping out milestone represents a significant step toward delivering one of the largest residential investments in TCU’s history. The project is part of a master plan for the Fort Worth school that has a budget of $500 million. bullets: TCU, American Campus Communities, Beck Group marked topping out on 2,500-bed on-campus housing.

stories.summary: Texas Christian University (in partnership with American Campus Communities and The Beck Group) reached topping out on a major on-campus residential development delivering 2,500+ beds split between pod-style first-year halls and townhome-style upper-division housing. The project is designed by Robert A.M. Stern Architects and is expected to open Fall 2027 as part of a $500 million TCU campus master plan. The university will retain ownership under a third-party fee-based development structure.
stories.impact: Institutional/student housing demand signal for Fort Worth: TCU's $500M capital commitment and 2,500-bed delivery by 2027 signals strong enrollment confidence and off-campus housing demand. Developers should monitor secondary student-housing opportunities near TCU's campus and competitive institutions (SMU, other DFW schools); ACC's involvement also confirms institutional appetite for long-term student-housing partnerships in growth markets.

stories.title: Camden Property Trust Completes Largest U.S Multifamily Sale Since 2024
stories.excerpt: JLL Capital Markets said Wednesday it had arranged the $1.625-billion sale and financed a significant portion of the portfolio of an 11-property, 3,620-unit multifamily portfolio spanning Southern California’s most supply-constrained submarkets. The transaction by Camden Property Trust represents the largest U.S. apartment sale since 2024, according to JLL. The buyer was a BlackRock-managed vehicle. The portfolio represents 16.5% of Southern California’s five-year average annual transaction volume by unit count in markets traditionally characterized by long-term ownership strategies. Properties in the portfolio include The Camden in Hollywood’s entertainment district; Camden Crown Valley, a 380-unit community in Mission Viejo; Camden Landmark, a 469-unit offering controlling 5% of Ontario’s entire market-rate inventory over 100 units; and Camden Hillcrest, a 132-unit boutique community delivered in 2021 in San Diego’s Hillcrest neighborhood. JLL’s Capital Markets’ Sales and Advisory team was led by senior managing director and Multi-Housing Platform leader Blake A. Rogers, managing directors Alexandra Caniglia and Kip Malo and senior director Dillon Bergum. The Debt Advisory team, led by Capital Markets president Kevin Mackenzie, managing directors Annie Rice and Brandon Smith, director Gyasi Edmondson and associate Alyssa Malley. arranged $566.6 million in agency acquisition financing on behalf of the buyer, secured by seven of the portfolio’s assets. The five-year fixed-rate loan is full-term interest only and was structured on an uncrossed basis, so each asset retains independent sale and refinance optionality. bullets: Camden Property Trust sold 11-property, 3,620-unit SoCal portfolio to BlackRock vehicle for $1.625B.
Largest U.S. apartment sale since 2024; properties in Hollywood, Mission Viejo, Ontario, San Diego.
Portfolio represents 16.5% of SoCal's 5-year average annual transaction volume by unit count.
stories.summary: Camden Property Trust completed a $1.625 billion sale of an 11-property, 3,620-unit multifamily portfolio across Southern California's supply-constrained submarkets to a BlackRock-managed vehicle, marking the largest U.S. apartment transaction since 2024. The portfolio includes flagship assets (The Camden Hollywood, Camden Crown Valley in Mission Viejo, Camden Landmark in Ontario controlling 5% of that market's 100+ unit inventory, and Camden Hillcrest in San Diego). JLL Capital Markets arranged and financed a significant portion of the deal.
stories.impact: Major signal of institutional capital (BlackRock) consolidating premium SoCal assets; transaction size and buyer profile suggest sustained appetite for supply-constrained CA markets despite macro uncertainty. For developers: BlackRock's $1.625B acquisition signals continued valuation resilience in Los Angeles, Orange County, Inland Empire, and San Diego—validate land deals and entitlements in these markets before 2027 deliveries; monitor if Camden's exit signals any concerns about near-term California rent growth or cap-rate expansion risk.

stories.title: JLL, Cousins Link Up on Two Austin Office Transactions
stories.excerpt: JLL Capital Markets completed two Austin, Texas, transactions with Cousins Properties. JLL arranged the sale of Research Park Plaza V, a 172,854-square-foot office building in Austin’s Northwest submarket, and secured a preferred equity placement for 5th & Walsh, a 198,000-square-foot Class A office and retail development in the West 5th Street corridor.  In the Research Park Plaza V sale, JLL Capital Markets’ Ryan Stevens, Drew Fuller and Jeff Coddington represented Cousins Properties to complete the sale to an unnamed buyer.  Developed in 2015, Research Park Plaza V is a Class A, four-story office asset that is 85% leased to four institutional-quality tenants.  For the 5th and Walsh development, JLL Capital Markets’ Stevens, Robert Wooten and Colby Mueck worked on behalf of Endeavor Real Estate Group (the developer) to arrange a $31.5 million preferred equity commitment through Cousins Properties. It will be Endeavor’s HQ. 5th & Walsh is a five-story, ground-up development totaling 198,000 rentable square feet, comprising approximately 177,000 square feet of Class A office and approximately 21,000 square feet of ground-floor retail. stories.impact: Not material to multifamily. Office transactions signal Austin's continued office-market activity and capital availability, but don't directly affect apartment supply, demand, or cost. However, sustained office development and mixed-use investment (5th & Walsh includes retail) support downtown Austin multifamily demand indirectly; developers should track office-to-residential conversion opportunities if these office projects underperform post-lease.

stories.title: Cushman & Wakefield Sets Second-Quarter Revenue Record
stories.excerpt: Cushman & Wakefield said Wednesday that its second-quarter earnings were strong enough to boost the commercial real estate services giant’s per-share earnings guidance for the year. “Our results this year demonstrated that we have hit our stride, and we’ve gotten there fast,” C&W CEO Michelle MacKay said Wednesday during the company’s earnings call. “We didn’t just meet the bar this quarter; we moved it, setting several company records, including the highest second-quarter total revenue in the history of the company, the highest second-quarter leasing and services revenue in the history of the company, and the lowest gross debt balance in the history of the company.” Revenue for the second quarter of 2026 grew by 11 percent year over year to $2.8 billion, while adjusted diluted earnings per share (EPS) grew 17 percent annually to 35 cents per share. C&W’s revenue for the second quarter of 2026 topped the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 4.6 percent, while EPS just missed the 36 cents per share analysts were expecting. “We achieved our sixth consecutive quarter of double-digit adjusted EPS growth. Back in December, at our investor day, we laid out our current three-year growth plan and provided annual EPS targets. Today, just two quarters later, we are raising our guidance for year one,” MacKay said during the call. “And here’s what excites us most: This performance is organic, driven by a global platform with significant white space still ahead.” Annual adjusted earnings per share guidance has been adjusted to reflect expected growth of between 18 percent and 23 percent, compared with C&W’s previous guidance of between 15 percent and 20 percent growth for the year. Leasing activity was strong this quarter, with leasing revenue growing by 27 percent year-over-year to $628.5 million. bullets: Cushman & Wakefield reported Q2 2026 revenue of $2.8B, up 11% YoY; adjusted EPS 35 cents.

stories.summary: Cushman & Wakefield reported record second-quarter 2026 total revenue of $2.8 billion (up 11% year-over-year) and adjusted diluted earnings per share of 35 cents (up 17% annually), beating Zacks consensus revenue by 4.6%. The company set multiple company records and reduced gross debt to historic lows, prompting CEO Michelle MacKay to raise full-year earnings guidance.
stories.impact: Positive market signal: strong CRE brokerage and capital-markets performance (especially record leasing/services revenue) indicates robust transaction velocity and capital flow in residential, office, and industrial. For developers: healthy broker economics = active capital, strong leasing momentum, and investor appetite for both acquisitions and new development financing. Monitor C&W's residential transaction commentary for early signals of market sentiment on multifamily supply, rent growth, and cap rates.

stories.title: Zenith IOS, JPMAM Seal $215M Credit Facility With KeyBank, Truist
stories.excerpt: Zenith IOS, JPMAM Seal $215M Credit Facility With KeyBank, Truist As the industrial outdoor storage space continues to gain momentum, some key players are celebrating the next phase of their partnership with a fresh round of financing. Zenith Industrial Outdoor Storage and J.P. Morgan Asset Management (JPMAM) just secured a $215 million credit facility from KeyBank and Truist, Commercial Observer can first report. The facility finances Zenith’s second programmatic joint venture with JPMAM and will allow the continued scaling of its expanding IOS portfolio. KeyBank served as administrative agent on the senior secured facility — which includes an accordion feature, allowing the JV to increase its borrowing capacity as needed — and led the transaction, while Truist served as joint lead arranger. Cooper-Horowitz’s Justin Horowitz, Ben Knopf and Josh Tropper arranged the facility. “This credit facility marks another significant milestone in our ongoing partnership with J.P. Morgan Asset Management, and reflects the continued institutional belief in the IOS sector,” Ben Atkins, co-founder and CEO of Zenith, said in a statement. “The scale and flexibility of this financing will allow us to accelerate acquisitions, deepen our presence in key growth markets, and continue executing on our long-term investment strategy. We are excited to build upon the success of our first joint venture and further strengthen this second programmatic partnership.” The facility refinances 34 IOS assets spanning 140 acres. The majority of the properties are spread across Southeast, South Central and Southwest markets, and the portfolio is almost fully leased at 99.6 percent. It’s not the first time the JV has teamed up with KeyBank. In February, the lender also provided a $130 million credit facility to Zenith and JPMAM for a portfolio of 14 IOS properties. stories.summary: Zenith Industrial Outdoor Storage (IOS) and J.P. KeyBank served as administrative agent and led the transaction; Truist was joint lead arranger. The facility includes an accordion feature allowing borrowing-capacity increases.
stories.impact: Not material to multifamily. Industrial outdoor storage is a distinct asset class (self-storage adjacent, non-residential). However, strong IOS/alternative asset financing activity signals robust regional/alternative lending by KeyBank and Truist; confirms capital-markets depth for non-traditional CRE. Monitor if alternative-asset strength draws capital away from multifamily financing or if it signals overall constructive credit availability for real-estate development more broadly.
